text:
leah: opening an escalation for a paying customer (C-45321). they see intermittent 502/504s when hitting the hosted inference endpoint (api.redwood.ai/v1/generate) starting ~2026-03-14 20:12 UTC. errors spike ~every 5-10 minutes for a few minutes, then clear. customer reports it started during our cert rotation window.

inc-bot: New escalation created: C-45321 (severity P1) — assigned to Support. See ticket link: https://zendesk.example/tickets/45321 :rotating_light:

leah: reproducer notes from customer (copied):
```
# repro (from customer's infra)
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"r/mid","input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (13.32.145.67) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering h2
* TLS handshake completed, but then curl returns:
* Received HTTP/2 stream 0 error: PROTOCOL_ERROR
* Closing connection 0
curl: (92) HTTP/2 stream 0 was not closed cleanly: PROTOCOL_ERROR (err 92)
```
They also attached an openssl s_client snapshot showing a partial handshake that times out after ServerHello (server sends no cert or connection reset) — looks like a truncation mid-handshake for some requests.

leah: customer tried alternate network and saw success. they ran `dig` from two resolvers and one of them intermittently returned SERVFAIL for the CNAME chain to our edge domain:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> api.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood.ai.  60 IN CNAME api-edge-us-east.redwood.ai.
api-edge-us-east.redwood.ai.  30 IN A 13.32.145.67

; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> api.redwood.ai @1.1.1.1
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 54321
;; WARNING: recursion requested but not available
```

jordan: :eyes: thanks leah. this feels like a mix of resolver flapping + some TCP/TLS truncation (could be PMTU/fragmentation or an upstream proxy closing mid-handshake). possible causes: bad resolver caching returning stale glue during cert rollout, or a middlebox dropping large TLS ClientHello/ServerHello fragments (EC keys + SNI + OCSP stapling can enlarge packets).

devin: can we get the following from the impacted customer IPs (or at least one repro client):
- tcpdump on edge for client IP 1-2 minutes around a failure (port 443), rotate pcap
- `tracepath <customer-ip>` or `mtu -s` from their host (to check PMTU)
- `dig +trace api.redwood.ai` and `dig @<their-resolver> api.redwood.ai` when they see SERVFAIL
- the full `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.ai:443 -servername api.redwood.ai -status -tlsextdebug` output

maya: runtime note — during cert rotation we send new chain to edges, and OCSP stapling refresh can create a slightly larger cert response. if there's an intermediate that fragments large TLS records and a firewall that blocks fragments or has small reassembly window, we can see mid-handshake failures. also ensure the edge is sending stapled OCSP; if a resolver returns SERVFAIL for the CNAME we might route to a different POP and hit a node with slightly different config.

leah: attaching the customer's tcpdump excerpt they provided (they redacted payloads):
```
# tcpdump snippet (client->edge)
18:12:05.123456 IP client > api-edge: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 1234 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
18:12:05.123457 IP api-edge > client: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 28960, options [mss 1460], length 0
18:12:05.123460 IP client > api-edge: Flags [P.], seq 1:1200, ack 1, length 1199  # large ClientHello
18:12:05.123472 IP api-edge > client: Rst
```
Their trace shows a large ClientHello (1199 bytes) then immediate RST from our edge. that lines up with either our edge process killing the connection (e.g., upstream worker failing to parse) or an intermediate node returning RST.

jordan: can we check the edge node's ssl_error_log and kern logs for OOM/oom_killer or worker restarts around 18:12:05? also want to see nginx upstream ssl_handshake_timeout entries. put links to logs here once available.

devin: on infra side — i pulled the config diffs from the canary cert rollout earlier. nothing obvious: nginx config unchanged, haproxy unchanged. but we do see increased rate of handshake timeouts on a small % of nodes in us-east-1 during the 20:00-20:30 window. i suspect a resolver propagation quirk put a subset of customers on a node behind a different NAT path which is flaky.

leah: customer confirms that when they set `--resolve api.redwood.ai:443:13.32.145.67` in curl they no longer see the error (bypass DNS) — points to DNS/resolver as at least part of it.

maya: mitigation options:
- temporarily increase handshake timeout and accept slightly lower hard-latency SLO to reduce resets
- enable fallback routing to previous cert-serving pool (roll traffic off nodes with higher error rates)
- disable OCSP stapling for a short window to shrink record size (tradeoff: increased OCSP latency)

jordan: prefer traffic shift + tcpdump capture. increasing handshake timeout could hide a real failure. also want to correlate which resolvers returned SERVFAIL and route those IPs to healthy nodes if possible.

devin: i can stage a route rule to divert traffic from the problematic node group to the healthy pool. need a timestamp window and a list of impacted client IPs. also will start packet capture on the node group (will post pcap link).

leah: asked customer to run these two quick checks and paste results here:
1) `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.ai:443 -servername api.redwood.ai -status -tlsextdebug` (post full output)
2) `dig @<their-nameserver> api.redwood.ai +short && dig +trace api.redwood.ai`

customer-rep: done — attached outputs. their 2nd resolver returned SERVFAIL consistently for 15 minutes. they also ran `tracepath` which showed a small MTU on one hop (1280) caused by a tunnel in their provider; but other routes were 1500. so this is intermittent depending on routing. they said re-running the same curl from a different vlan (no tunnel) worked.

maya: aha — so PMTU differences plus a big ClientHello can trigger fragmentation and if any middlebox blocks fragmented TLS records we see mid-handshake failures. plus if DNS picks a different POP (due to resolver returning SERVFAIL) you can land on the POP that has both the new cert + slightly different network path -> reproduces.

jordan: recommended temporary steps:
- devin: route affected IPs to healthy pool (deprioritize the node group) — block window 30m
- devin: start tcpdump on affected nodes and upload pcaps
- maya: prepare rollback of cert or enable serving old chain on nodes to avoid large handshake packet variation
- leah: ask customer to pin A record (workaround) and share their resolver ip(s)

devin: done — route rule applied at 21:05 UTC. tcpdump started and pcaps uploaded to s3://redwood-support/pcaps/C-45321/

maya: i pushed a config to serve the older chain for nodes in the problematic pool at 21:12 UTC (canary). monitoring for handshake resets.

jordan: monitoring graph — handshake timeouts dropped from 0.8% -> 0.15% after traffic shift and old-chain canary. still keep collecting pcaps for 60m.

leah: customer updated — errors stopped after we applied route rule and canary (they confirmed at 21:20 UTC). they will keep an eye and will try to adjust their resolver or MTU on their side.

devin: action items (owner:devin): upload full pcaps, list of impacted client IPs, config diffs for canary rollback — will do within 2h.

maya: action items (owner:maya): run a quick audit for cert chain size and consider temporarily disabling stapling when PMTU < 1400 for connections (maybe we can implement record-size shrink as short term). follow up in eng-runtime.

leah: closing loop with customer, noted workaround and next steps. will convert to internal postmortem if we see recurrence. thanks team :heart:

jordan: adding note — follow-up: run a DNS propagation analysis for our cert rotation windows and consider adding staggered rollouts per resolver heatmap. next sync with infra & runtime tomorrow 10:00 UTC. :calendar:

leah: marking ticket C-45321 as mitigated. will update ticket with steps and link to pcaps.
